zh: 我还有一个激进观点，是我对 AGI 的一个定义。

zh: 而 AGI 是出了名的难以定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does it mean for it to be artificial general intelligence?
zh: 成为人造通用智能意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The Turing test was one, but we'd pretty much blown past the Turing test in a lot of ways.
zh: 图灵测试是其中之一，但我们在很多方面已经大大超过了图灵测试。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我们没有一个好的定义。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I have noticed is that you can tell how much better AI is getting by how long a leash you can give it to do work.
zh: 所以我注意到的是，你可以通过你可以给它多长的“绳子”去工作来判断 AI 变好了多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with Copilot, you can tab complete and that was the beginning.
zh: 比如用 Copilot，你可以进行 Tab 补全，那就是开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: With ChatGPT, you ask it a question and it returns a response and that's maybe slightly better than a tab complete.
zh: 用 ChatGPT，你问它一个问题，它返回一个回答，这可能比 Tab 补全稍微好一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then now with Claude Opus 4 and Gemini and all that kind of stuff, also with deep research, it can go off and work for 20 or 30 minutes.
zh: 而现在用 Claude Opus 4 和 Gemini 以及所有这类东西，还有深度研究，它可以离开并工作 20 或 30 分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that leash is getting longer where you have to intervene.
zh: 那个“绳子”正在变长，直到你必须介入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was thinking about this and it reminded me of Winnicott, who was a child psychologist.
zh: 我在思考这个问题，它让我想起了 Winnicott，他是一位儿童心理学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wrote this book called Playing & Reality.
zh: 他写了这本书叫《游戏与现实》。

speaker: Unknown
en: And his conceptualization for what it means to become an adult, what it means to go from being an infant to a child to an adult is when you're first born, you're effectively fused with usually your mother, your caregiver.
zh: 他对成为成年人意味着什么，对从婴儿变成孩子再变成成年人意味着什么的概念化是，当你刚出生时，你实际上与通常是你的母亲、你的照料者融合在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no difference between you and her or you and whoever your caregiver is.
zh: 你和她之间，或者你和你的照料者之间没有区别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And growing up is this process of being gradually let down in certain moments where you can handle being let down.
zh: 成长就是这样一个过程，在特定的时刻被逐渐放下，在这些时刻你能处理被放下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you learn that there's a separation between you and your caregiver.
zh: 所以你了解到你和你的照料者之间存在分离。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for infants, it's instead of being fused at the hip for every hour of every day, you get left alone.
zh: 对于婴儿来说，不再是一天中的每一小时都和大人形影不离，而是会被单独留下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe you get left alone to cry it out.
zh: 也许你被单独留下哭着去解决问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows if that's the right thing to do with infants?
zh: 谁知道这对婴儿是不是正确的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of consternation there.
zh: 那里有很多担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's teaching you that there's a separation between you and your mom or you and your dad.
zh: 但那是在教你，你和你妈妈或你爸爸之间存在分离。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not going to always be someone to pick you up.
zh: 不会总有人来抱你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And raising a child is about knowing when they're ready to be let down a little bit and have to stand up on their own.
zh: 抚养孩子就是关于知道他们什么时候准备好被稍微放下一点，不得不自己站起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's that same leash with human development.
zh: 所以我认为人类发展也有同样的那条“绳子”。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get longer and longer periods of time where you can be on your own.
zh: 你会有越来越长的时间段可以独处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're still in the 20 to 30 minutes is maybe... I don't know, you probably can't leave a toddler alone for 20 or 30 minutes, but it's a little bit older than a toddler.
zh: 所以我们还在 20 到 30 分钟的阶段，这可能是……我不知道，你可能无法把一个刚学步的小孩单独留下 20 或 30 分钟，但这比刚学步的孩子稍微大一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe 20, 30 seconds.

zh: 对于一个刚学步的孩子，你可以在同一个房间，但在 20 分钟里有时不需要每秒都和他们互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's around there.
zh: 所以就在那个阶段左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have that similar leash with AGI.
zh: 我认为我们对 AGI 也有类似的“绳子”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think a good definition of AGI is when does it become economically profitable for people to run agents indefinitely?
zh: 所以我认为 AGI 的一个好的定义是，什么时候让智能体无限期地运行在经济上是变得有利可图的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it just never turns off.
zh: 所以它永远不会关闭。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a Claude Code that's always running, it's always doing something, you just never turn it off, and you don't need to because you know that it's worthwhile to keep it on.
zh: 这是一个始终运行的 Claude Code，它总是在做些什么，你只需永不关闭它，而且你也无需关闭，因为你知道让它保持开启是值得的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's never waiting for you to be like, "Okay, next thing."
zh: 它从不等着你来说，“好的，下一件事。”

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll always respond to you when you're like, "Okay, next thing."
zh: 但当你说，“好的，下一件事”时，它总是会响应你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's off just essentially living its life like a teenager and that is profitable for you.
zh: 但它基本上就像一个青少年一样过着自己的生活，这对你是有利可图的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'd rather have it do that than just wait for you to tell it what to do next.
zh: 你宁愿它那样做，而不是等着你告诉它下一步要做什么。

speaker: Lenny

zh: 我认为这是 AGI 的一个很好的定义。

en: The profitable piece is also just the cost of running that thing and having it.
zh: 有利可图的部分也仅仅是运行那个东西并拥有它的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's partly the cost and partly the value.
zh: 部分是成本，部分是价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously, you can game this a little bit and be like, "Cool, I'm just going to tell Claude to run in a loop forever."
zh: 显然，你可以稍微利用这一点，然后说，“酷，我就要告诉 Claude 永远在循环中运行。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm talking about more than that, more widespread adoption of agents that work all the time.
zh: 但我指的不止这些，而是更广泛地采用始终工作的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I like the profitable thing, because if it costs a little bit of money and the bar is profitability, it has to actually be doing something useful for you to keep it on.
zh: 我喜欢那个有利可图的说法，因为如果它花一点钱，而门槛是盈利能力，那么它必须实际上在为你做有用的事情你才会让它保持开启。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting how the metaphor of a senior employee and autonomy and essentially the more autonomous they are, the less instruction you have to give, the less reviews you have to do, is also just directly correlated with how senior they are.
zh: 资深员工和自主性的比喻很有趣，本质上它们越自主，你需要给的指示就越少，你需要做的审查就越少，这也直接与它们的资深程度相关。

en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

en: I hate the headlines that are like, "It's going to replace jobs," or "It's going to unemploy two thirds of the workforce."
zh: 我讨厌那些诸如“它将取代工作”或“它将使三分之二的劳动力失业”的标题。

zh: 我不认为那是真的。

zh: 我讨厌那些诸如“使用 ChatGPT 时你不用动脑”的标题，或者另一个好标题是，“只有医生，医生加 AI，或者只有 AI，哪个更好？

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is better, therefore, doctors are going to be outmoded."
zh: AI 更好，因此，医生将被淘汰。”

speaker: Unknown
en: All that stuff is, I think, pretty dumb.
zh: 所有这些事情，我认为，都很愚蠢。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for the doctors plus AI example, I think it's important to recognize that using AI is a skill.
zh: 所以对于医生加 AI 的例子，我认为重要的是要认识到使用 AI 是一项技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you study doctors in a vacuum that don't really have a lot of experience with AI, you could probably create a situation such that it's better to just use an AI.
zh: 因此，如果你研究那些真正没有太多 AI 经验的医生，你可能会制造出一种情况，即只使用 AI 会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes it is going to be better.
zh: 而且有时它确实会更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's so many contexts that doctors need to make decisions and do things that it's really hard to take one study and make any conclusion about that.
zh: 但是医生需要做出决定和做事情的语境太多了，很难仅凭一项研究就对此得出任何结论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's especially hard when you're dealing with a technology that's developing so rapidly that doctors can't really be expected to be experts at it yet.
zh: 尤其是当你面对一种发展如此之快的技术时，医生们还不可能真正成为这方面的专家，这就更难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I would guess in five or 10 years, that will be totally and completely different.
zh: 但我猜在 5 年或 10 年后，情况将完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the student example or the "AI turns your brain off" example, I think it's really important to understand that in the history of technology, it has always been the case that you give up certain skills in order to get other ones.
zh: 对于学生的例子或者“AI 让你的大脑停摆”的例子，我认为理解这一点非常重要：在技术史上，为了获得其他技能，你总是要放弃某些技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, Plato is famously very skeptical of writing because he thought it would harm your memory.
zh: 例如，柏拉图 famously 对写作持怀疑态度，因为他认为这会损害你的记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it did.
zh: 事实也确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't remember things quite as well as they did back in the day because they had to remember long epic poems to entertain each other.
zh: 我们记忆事物的效果不如过去的人好，因为他们必须背诵长长的史诗诗歌来互相娱乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think writing is a worthwhile trade for having a slightly worse memory.
zh: 但我认为为了拥有稍微差一点的记忆力，写作是一个值得的交换。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think something similar is going on with AI where you may be slightly less engaged in certain tasks, but if you use it right, you're going to be way more engaged in other tasks where you have much more power.
